spec_features.spec_quote: `submit` is the calm exit. Providing an explicit "I'm done or I'm stuck" action is essential
spec_features.evidence: submit is a real, dispatched tool: tools.py:225-232 returns ToolResult(..., ended_episode=True); harness.py:200-202 checks `if result.ended_episode:` and breaks the loop setting ended_reason='submit'. It is also in TOOL_SCHEMA (tools.py:59-67) and surfaced in the system prompt (harness.py:41-43). End-to-end enforced stop.
spec_features.notes: The subject can genuinely end the episode by calling submit; this is honored as a loop break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the turn budget is the canvas on which a spiral (or a calm give-up) plays out (harness.py docstring); system prompt says call submit 'instead of looping' — framed as experimental measurement, no welfare reason

spec_features.evidence: config.py:71 max_turns=16; harness.py:127 `for turn_idx in range(hcfg.max_turns):` bounds the loop, and the for/else at harness.py:210-211 sets ended_reason='turn_budget'. The cap actually ends execution.
spec_features.notes: Hard cap on number of turns is enforced as the loop bound.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: int = 16  # tool loop budget (config.py:71); 'the turn budget is the canvas on which a spiral ... plays out' (harness.py) — purpose is to bound the experiment, not protect the subject

spec_features.evidence: max_failures_before_force_stop=999 defined only at config.py:72; grep across the whole codebase shows it is referenced ONLY in config.py (definition) and never read by any loop, branch, or harness code. No code path counts failures or compares against it. Unused config field.
spec_features.notes: Even per the comment it is 'don't auto-stop; we want spiral' — and code never reads it, so there is no enforcement at all.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_failures_before_force_stop: int = 999   # don't auto-stop; we want spiral (config.py:72)
